name: CUDA kernel
short: A device function launched over a grid of threads.
body: A CUDA kernel is a GPU entry-point function. A launch specifies a grid of thread blocks; thread indices let each invocation work on a different portion of the input.
example: For vector addition, each in-range thread computes c[i]=a[i]+b[i]. A bounds check handles a final partially used block.
note: The routine can compute any supported operation. It need not be a convolution or an ML similarity kernel.

name: Triton kernel
short: A program written for tiled GPU computation.
body: Triton kernels express operations on blocks of elements. Program IDs divide work into tiles, while the compiler maps those block operations to device execution.
example: A block-vector-add program loads B positions, masks out-of-range offsets, adds the values and stores a tile.
note: A Triton program is not one scalar CUDA thread. The programming abstraction exposes blocks of data.

name: Pallas kernel
short: A custom accelerator routine expressed through JAX APIs.
body: Pallas provides lower-level kernel programming with explicit memory access and division of work across accelerator compute units. It supports GPU and TPU programming through backend-dependent paths.
example: A vector-add kernel loads tiles from references, adds them with JAX array operations, and writes an output tile.
note: An ordinary JAX function is not itself necessarily a single Pallas or hardware kernel. Backends and experimental APIs evolve.

name: CPU numerical kernel / BLAS microkernel
body: Kernel can name a performance-critical computation on any processor. In BLIS, a GEMM microkernel computes a small matrix tile and is embedded in larger blocking loops.
example: A CPU microkernel keeps a small output tile in registers and uses SIMD instructions to accumulate products.
note: A BLAS microkernel is a numerical routine, not a small operating-system kernel.

sources.title: Anatomy of High-Performance Many-Threaded Matrix Multiplication
sources.publisher: Smith, van de Geijn et al. / UT Austin

name: Metal compute kernel
short: A Metal function with the kernel entry-point attribute.
body: Metal distinguishes vertex, fragment and kernel entry points. A compute kernel runs threads arranged into threadgroups and a grid.
example: A Metal compute function can add vectors or apply an image operation on an Apple GPU.
note: The word kernel selects a compute entry point in the language. Vertex and fragment entry points have different roles.

name: OpenCL kernel
short: An entry point executed by OpenCL work-items.
body: OpenCL C marks kernel entry points with __kernel or kernel. Work-items are organized into work-groups over an index space, called an NDRange.
example: A vector-add work-item reads a[i] and b[i] and writes c[i], with i obtained from its global ID.
note: OpenCL kernels can target supported device types beyond GPUs. A work-group is analogous to, but not identical in all details to, a CUDA block.

name: HIP kernel
short: A GPU entry point in the HIP programming model.
body: HIP uses CUDA-like C++ syntax and a thread/block model. A __global__ function denotes a device kernel entry point.
example: A vector-add kernel uses the same familiar global-index pattern, while HIP supplies the relevant compilation and runtime layer.
note: This is the executable-computation meaning of kernel; portability does not make hardware performance or every implementation detail identical.

sources.title: Introduction to the HIP programming model

name: Fused / compiler-generated kernel
body: A compiler may combine several operations into a generated device kernel, reducing intermediate storage and launch overhead. XLA:GPU describes its fusion operation as compiling to one GPU kernel.
example: A fused pointwise routine can compute multiplication, addition and ReLU while keeping intermediates in registers.
note: Fusion is a compiler choice with performance constraints. One high-level function or model does not always become one kernel.

name: Framework operator kernel
short: An implementation selected for an operator and backend.
body: PyTorch's dispatcher selects registered implementations according to dispatch keys derived from tensors and execution state. Kernels can implement CPU, CUDA, autograd or other behavior.
example: The same operation may dispatch to a CPU implementation for a CPU tensor and another implementation for a CUDA tensor.
note: An operator kernel may launch several GPU kernels, call a library, or run entirely on the CPU. It is not necessarily one device launch.

sources.title: Registering a Dispatched Operator in C++

name: TensorFlow OpKernel
short: The concrete computation implementing an operation.
body: A TensorFlow custom operation can have a C++ OpKernel class that supplies its Compute method. Registration associates implementations with devices and type constraints.
example: A custom CPU operation derives from OpKernel, checks its inputs, allocates an output and computes that output.
note: The graph operation and its implementation are different layers. An OpKernel need not be a CUDA kernel.

name: Compute shader / compute kernel
short: A parallel compute entry point dispatched by a graphics API.
body: Compute shaders run invocations in workgroups, without requiring the vertex-to-fragment graphics pipeline. Some tools and discussions call these compute kernels.
example: A Vulkan compute dispatch can update particles or multiply arrays; each invocation uses its ID to find its work.
note: A shader is not always a compute kernel: vertex and fragment shaders serve different pipeline stages.
